draft.title: Weighing a scientific solution
card: A science-based solution to a problem can have effects beyond fixing the problem. People judge it by looking at four kinds of effect before it is used.
Ethical asks if it is right and fair, including how it treats animals and people. Environmental asks what it might do to living things, soil, water and air.
Social asks how it affects people and communities. Economic asks what it costs and who gains or loses money.
Bringing in a new species to control a pest is one example. The new species might spread and eat native plants, which is an environmental effect.
draft.remember: A solution can be judged on all its effects, not only whether it fixes the problem.

a.q: Why is a solution judged on its ethical, environmental, social and economic effects?
opts: It may fix one problem but cause others
It will be cheap if it is judged this way
It will be accepted if it is judged this way
It proves the idea is new to scientists
a.why: A solution can work on the problem and still cause harm in other ways, so all four kinds of effect are checked. Cost is only the economic effect, and judging does not make a solution cheap.
a.clue: Think about what else a solution might change.

b.q: A council plans to bring a new insect into Tasmania to eat a weed. Scientists say it might also eat native plants. Which kind of effect is this?
opts: An environmental effect
An economic effect
A social effect
An ethical effect
b.why: Harm to native plants is an effect on living things in the environment. It could also lead to costs or worries for people, but the effect described is on the plants themselves.
b.clue: Which effect is about plants and animals in nature?

a.best: It may fix one problem but cause others

problems.detail: The right option is the only one hedged with 'may'. The three wrong options all make absolute claims ('will be cheap', 'will be accepted', 'proves'), so a test-wise student could pick the answer without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Weighing a scientific solution
card: A science-based solution to a problem can have effects beyond fixing the problem. People judge it by looking at four kinds of effect before it is used.
Ethical asks if it is right and fair, including how it treats animals and people. Environmental asks what it might do to living things, soil, water and air.
Social asks how it affects people and communities. Economic asks what it costs and who gains or loses money.
Cane toads were brought to Queensland in 1935 to eat beetles on sugar cane. They spread widely and poisoned native animals that ate them, which is an environmental effect.
proposal.remember: A solution can be judged on all its effects, not only whether it fixes the problem.

a.q: Why do people check a solution's ethical, environmental, social and economic effects?
opts: It can fix one problem but cause harm in other ways
It can be judged on cost alone if it works well
It can be used without checks if scientists made it
It can only be checked once it is already in use
a.why: A solution can work on the problem and still cause harm in other ways, so all four kinds of effect are checked before it is used. Looking at cost alone would miss effects on people, animals and the environment.
a.clue: Think about what else a solution might change.
